Document.project_name: Shorepine Bog Trail Revitalization
location: Pacific Rim National Park Reserve of Canada
Document.description: The Shorepine Bog Trail is an approximately 800 m loop boardwalk, originally constructed in 1986, that provides a short, immersive experience through a rare and sensitive coastal bog ecosystem in Pacific Rim National Park Reserve. Over time, the boardwalk has deteriorated, resulting in uneven surfaces, misaligned sections, abrupt elevation changes, and damaged treads. These conditions have reduced accessibility, and the trail no longer meets current accessibility standards. This project proposes to replace the existing boardwalk with a fully accessible structure elevated above the bog. Once completed, the upgraded Shorepine Bog Trail will provide a barrier-free opportunity for visitors to explore and appreciate this unique coastal environment. Parks Canada will complete a Basic Impact Assessment to assess the potential impacts of the project on ecological and cultural values and identify mitigation measures to avoid or minimize adverse impacts.

Document.project_name: Power System Replacement, Helipad Construction, and Soil Remediation at Sand Hill River Counting Facility, Labrador
Document.proponent: Fisheries and Oceans Canada – Real Property and Environmental Management (DFO-RPEM)
Document.description: The proposed project at the Sand Hill River Counting Facility includes: the removal, relocation, and replacement of the electrical building; upgrades to the existing electrical systems; the extension of the existing raised wooden walkway to facilitate access to the new electrical building; the construction of a new gravel helipad; the construction of a new walkway from the helipad to the existing walkway; the replacement of the fuel drop pad; and the remediation of contaminated soils. The new walkway from the new electrical building to the existing walkway will be installed on concrete blocks and raised above the ground with wood posts. The old electrical building will be demolished and removed. All materials will be disposed of at an appropriate disposal facility. The new electrical building will be installed in a similar fashion to the walkway – on concrete blocks and raised on wooden posts. The footprint of the new electrical building is approximately 20 square meters. The new helipad will be constructed of granular material compacted down into a 54 square meter area on the northern side of the property. The existing access route from the helipad to the site is an undeveloped footpath. The new walkway would be installed in the same route as the footpath with minimal tree cutting. The new walkway will be installed on concrete blocks and raised above the ground with wood posts. The existing fuel drop pad will be demolished and removed, then subsequently replaced with a new pressure-treated timber structure that will expand upon the existing footprint by approximately double. The area identified as containing  impacted surface soil is located on the easternmost area of the property.  The soil will be removed and transported off-site for treatment and disposal at a licensed soil recycling facility.

Document.project_name: Kahkewistahaw First Nation Community Landfill Reclamation
Document.description:
Kahkewistahaw First Nation is planning to reclaim the community's landfill. Future waste generated in the area will be disposed of at a new solid waste transfer station. The primary objective of the proposed work is to return the site to a state where it can be used for other activities and achieve site closure. Waste materials (solid waste, bulky metallic waste, and finished compost) will be buried and/or removed from the property prior to construction of a cap and cover system, which will be compacted and contoured to minimize infiltration and promote drainage. A clay cover will be overlain by topsoil and reseeded. Access to the site will be restricted upon landfill closure.

Site preparation activities include installation of a fence and locked gate, as well as cleanup of waste debris scattered throughout the site with redistribution into the waste pits, or off-site for disposal. Construction activities include collection of clay from a nearby source and transportation to the site. The waste pits will be covered and the landfill compacted and contoured to promote drainage. Once the cap has been constructed, a layer of topsoil, sourced locally, will be placed over the clay and reseeded using a local grass seed mix.

Document.project_name: Kinistin Saulteaux Nation Road Improvements
Document.description:
Kinistin Saulteaux Nation is proposing to improve approximately 15 km of main access, rural residential, and core area roadways located throughout the community. The proposed project involves surfacing repairs, ditch grading improvements, embankment upgrades, and four culvert crossings.

Site preparation activities include stripping topsoil within roadway ditches of the core residential area where ditching upgrades will be completed, as well as the south side of the Highway 773 embankment where sloping improvements will be completed. Construction activities will consist of excavating and filling existing roadway surfacing to design elevations, excavation of roadway to facilitate culvert installations, preparing existing subgrade materials, and application of aggregate and surfacing materials to the road surface. Following construction, disturbed areas will be restored with topsoil and seeding.

All anticipated waste generated during construction activities will be managed and disposed of at designated landfill facility. Procedures will be implemented throughout construction to prevent potential contamination from petroleum products used for on-site equipment.

Document.project_name: Town of Banff 26DP63 420 Muskrat Street Redevelopment
Document.description: The proponent proposes redeveloping 420 Muskrat Street from a single dwelling to the creation of 18 units. The development will include: demolition of existing single-family home, construction of 3 new buildings, installation of utilities and site landscaping.

Document.project_name: North Hardstands Phase 1
Document.description:
Proposed Project: North Hardstands Phase 1

As part of the Greater Toronto Airports Authority's (GTAA's) Toronto Pearson Airport Longterm Investment in Facilities & Terminals (LIFT) Program, the North Hardstand and associated infrastructure are proposed to be constructed on the Airfield.

The proposed development will be located airside near the east end of Runway 05-23, southwest of the intersection of Airport Road and Derry Road, on previously developed land with the function to process additional passengers and to serve as aircraft parking. The project will occur in phases, with Phase 1 beginning this year. Future phases are under consideration and, if progressed, will be posted separately. The Phase 1 project scope includes:


	Construction of approximately 200,000 square metres of pavement for aircraft parking and manoeuvring, with a total of 10 aircraft stands.
	2000 sq m ground service equipment (GSE) support building, a Triturator building, a Blast Fence, snow dump & melting area, and a Non-Passenger Screening – Vehicle structure. 
	Installation of high-mast lighting systems 
	Provision of hydrant fueling infrastructure 
	Development of a new connection to existing Taxiway Juliet 
	Implementation of new drainage infrastructure, including a stormwater retention system and oil/water interceptors to manage both quantity and quality of runoff.


Construction activities will involve excavation, clearing and grubbing, utility relocation and removal, site grading, installation of underground services, paving, line marking, lighting installation, and concrete works, along with supporting boarding infrastructure.

Sustainability best practices will be integrated into both the design and construction phases, aligning with the broader Long-Term Investment in Facilities and Terminals (LIFT) Program at Toronto Pearson Airport.

Note: Six of the 10 aircraft stands included in this project are designated for cargo operations and a separate project posting has also been made. Refer to reference number 90411.

Document.project_name: North Cargo Hardstands
Parks Canada Agency Whistlers Campground Exclusion Fence
Document.description: The Whistlers Campground Exclusion Fence Project will involve the installation of ungulate-exclusion fencing around the perimeter of Whistlers Campground in Jasper National Park. The project includes removal of conflict trees within the fence right-of-way, site preparation, installation of wooden post and page wire fencing, pedestrian gates, and cattle guards at vehicle access points. The fence is intended to reduce human-wildlife conflicts associated with elk use of the campground and support a safe camping experience for visitors.

Document.project_name: Range and Training Area Upgrades – Canadian Armed Forces Training Area (CAFTA) Cedar Springs
location: Canadian Armed Forces Training Area (CAFTA) Cedar Springs
Document.description:
The Department of National Defence (DND) proposes a project. The Canadian Armed Forces Training Area (CAFTA) Cedar Springs is an active training facility that runs approximately 70 training events per year with the expectation that this number will increase in the coming years. As such, the existing Cedar Springs Range and Training Area (RTA) is lacking the infrastructure to support the expected increase in training events at this site. Therefore, DND intends to upgrade the training area to be more consistent with the proposed future capabilities and are looking to improve the range infrastructure for the future training requirements.

The project activities include:

Backstop Berm Upgrades:


	Backstop berm work at the site involves the removal of existing sand pits, removal and replacement of the backstop, providing new wood borders around bullet catch areas and filling with rubber mulch and geotextile materials for the base of pits, in addition to grading, topsoiling and hydroseeding the work area.


Firing Range Upgrades


	The firing range upgrades include the installation of new coloured lane markers at firing points, replacement of the target numbers on the backstop berm and removal of existing firing point berms to meet the requirements of the DND Range Area Construction Manual.


Trenching Area and Confidence Course Work


	Trenching area work that will take place includes the installation of four wooden post markers to identify the trenching area.
	Confidence course work includes the replacement or reinstallation of the existing high wall, all rusted fasteners, wood planks on the bridge infrastructure, and securing the existing ramp box to supports.
	Obstacle (OB) infrastructure improvements include: The realignment of steel posts, the replacement of steels posts, and installation of tie-backs, the repair of timber planks, the reconnection of overhead bungee cords to timber posts, replacement of rusted wire rope, repairing rusted steel angle connections, replacement of deteriorated plywood, and the replacement of steel cable covers at top of timber posts.


Improvements to Site Drainage:


	Overall site drainage improvements throughout the firing range and confidence course area, directing water from this area to the existing drainage ditches to eliminate pooling issues.
	Natural enhancements to the site layout, such as improved sloping and diverting surface runoff toward swales. No underground services or catch basins will be installed as part of this project.


Additional Site Improvements:


	Installation of electrical infrastructure for existing wood pads used for tenting in the forward operating base (FOB).
	Extension of the southwest portion of the perimeter fence.
	Repair or replacement of existing sentry huts, if needed.
	Provision of new light poles with new high efficiency LED luminaries, controlled by a new centralized photocell and fed from the new main power panel of the base.
	Target shed construction behind firing butt area.

Document.project_name: Shoal Lake 40 First Nation Wastewater Treatment System
Document.description:
The project will involve the construction of a wastewater treatment system which will utilize Submerged Attached Growth Reactor (SAGR) treatment cells, with a grinder, microscreen, clarification, and UV disinfection located inside a proposed 380 square meter building. The treatment system will accept both hauled sewage from the existing septic tanks in the community and collected wastewater from piped services for future housing developments, designed for 20 years. A generator will be installed on the premises in case of power outages. The total footprint for development is approximately 10,000 square meters including the proposed buildling, SAGR cells, driveway, upgrades to the access road, waterwaste piping and borrow area.

The discharge of the system will be an above-ground outfall located adjacent to a wetland which connects to Snowshoe Bay in Shoal Lake. Shoal Lake is used as a drinking water source for the community and Winnipeg. The intakes for both these systems are in Indian Bay, on the opposite side of the Shoal Lake 40 peninsula. The treated effluent is expected to meet all effluent guidelines and not impact the water quality of Shoal Lake.

This project is in association with support from Infrastructure Canada's posting #89407.

Document.project_name: Department of National Defence, Strategic Tanker Transport Capability Project Support Infrastructure at CFB Trenton - Expansion of the existing Air Mobility Training Centre (AMTC) WP4
Document.description:
The Department of National Defence (DND) has proposed a project. DND is undertaking the expansion of the Air Mobility Training Centre (AMTC) in its northern section adjacent to Yukon Street, as well as renovation of parts of the existing AMTC. The construction footprint of the Project is approximately 1.67 ha (16,700 m2).
Project Components to be constructed in the Project Site include the following:


	AMTC expansion
	Renovation of parts of the existing AMTC building including a new east access into AMTC building and associated asphalt loading dock 
	Installation of new temporary crosswalks
	Resurfacing and patching
	Removal of existing asphalt
	New asphalt paving
	Concrete work
	Removal of existing landscaping and trees


The Project consists of the following phases:

Site Preparation: This phase will include tree clearing, vegetation removal, grubbing, and earthworks on the Project Site to prepare construction areas. Any trees kept on site will be protected by barricades to prevent damages. Soils to be reused for construction will be stockpiled. Unused soils will be handled in accordance with the governing regulations and will be stored in one of the stockpile locations. Temporary staging and laydown areas will be established. In addition, site preparation activities will also involve the installation of new temporary crosswalks to facilitate safe pedestrian movement during construction, as well as resurfacing and patching of the adjacent north parking lot to ensure continued accessibility and functionality for personnel and visitors.
Construction: This phase will include the construction of the AMTC expansion building. This phase will also include the removal of a wall on the eastern side of the AMTC building to accommodate the construction of a new eastern access, removal of existing asphalt and concrete to support the construction of an asphalt loading dock. In addition, ancillary project work includes managing contaminated soil, sediment, or groundwater, and addressing areas needing more vegetation removal or other impacts. Examples include roads, utilities, laydown, or storage spaces during construction.
Site Restoration: This phase will consist of reinstating and restoring all areas disturbed by the construction of the Project and the construction of compensatory restoration areas. This phase will be completed after completion of the construction phase. All areas disturbed during construction will be restored and stabilized (i.e., vegetated, landscaping) once associated construction activities are complete. All temporary measures, including silt fencing, dewatering systems, disposal bins, site trailers, lighting, tree barricades, and other general conditions, will be removed during this phase. In addition, a final clean-up will be conducted to address any remaining loose material on site.
Operations: During the operations phase, the proposed AMTC expansion will serve to provide additional capacity to train aircrew and support personnel in air mobility operations.
Decommissioning and Abandonment: No decommissioning phase is anticipated. In the unlikely event that the Project ceases to operate, DND would be responsible for decommissioning in accordance with applicable regulations as required at the time.

The anticipated project start date for site preparation is: February 2027
The anticipated in-service date (operations) is: December 2028

Document.project_name: Upgrade of the HMCS Brunswicker Jetty – Saint John, New Brunswick
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. The majority of work will involve concrete repairs to the vertical and horizontal surfaces of the jetty, caisson, floating dock and piles. This will include the removal of 25mm to 75mm of concrete and repairing with new polymer-modified mortar. Other miscellaneous work will also be included replacement of the timber fenders, replacement of the sacrificial anodes, installing and insulating a new water line and some other minor mechanical/electrical items.

Document.project_name: Parking Lot Repaving at Gateway Postal Facility Mississauga, ON
Document.description: This project will involve the rehabilitation and re-pavement of approximately 8,150 m² of the existing parking lot at the Gateway Postal Facility in Mississauga. The existing parking surface is showing signs of wear and requires rehabilitation to maintain safe and efficient site operations. The work will include removal and replacement of existing asphalt pavement, pavement markings, and associated site improvements. Construction staging will occur within the existing parking lot and will not extend beyond the current developed footprint. The project site is located within an existing urbanized and developed area. Wood Creek Park is located approximately 1.13 km west of the project site, and a watercourse is located approximately 1.2 km east of the site. Work will be staged in a phased approach.

Document.project_name: Big Island Cree Nation Road Upgrades and Repairs - Site 4

Document.project_name: Parking Lot Repaving at Toronto Pearson International Airport
Flood recovery and climate resilience in Pakistan
Document.description:
This project aims to address critical challenges caused or exacerbated by the 2022 floods while strengthening resilience to climate change and future shocks for flood-affected and at-risk communities. It will support proactive risk mitigation and gender-responsive disaster preparedness, response, and recovery measures, with a particular focus on the needs of women and girls. The project will also accelerate resilient access to and delivery of essential basic services and promote access to assets, resources, and strategies that are critical for restoring livelihoods and increasing long-term community resilience in flood-affected areas.

To achieve these objectives, the project will undertake a range of infrastructure rehabilitation and resilience-building works in high-risk and flood-impacted locations. Flood-damaged protective structures will be rehabilitated or upgraded to reduce vulnerability to future flooding. At-risk health facilities will be rehabilitated and retrofitted to ensure the continuity of essential healthcare services during climate-related events. Schools will be rehabilitated and/or retrofitted to provide safer learning environments, while drinking water supply and sanitation schemes will be restored and strengthened in flood-affected communities. In addition, flood-damaged irrigation channels will be rehabilitated to support agricultural production, restore livelihoods, and improve the resilience of local farming systems to future climate and disaster risks. Among others, physical works will include the installation of fences, water pipelines and crossing towers, as well as the rehabilitation of reservoir tanks, spring eye protection infrastructure and valve boxes.

The planned locations are in general characterized by mountainous and high-altitude environments comprising valleys, meadows, and sparsely vegetated slopes. The terrain is generally rugged, with steep gradients, and rocky, shallow, erosion-prone soils. Surface geology is often dominated by highly weathered rock formations, while landforms are shaped by rivers, seasonal streams, snowmelt, and other natural drainage systems. Water resources typically depend on springs, surface water channels, and seasonal runoff, with limited groundwater availability in many locations. The climate ranges from temperate to cold, with distinct seasonal variations that include prolonged winters, snowfall at higher elevations, and relatively short growing seasons. These areas are increasingly exposed to climate-related hazards, including extreme precipitation, flooding, slope instability, erosion, and landslides. Ongoing climate variability and changing hydrological patterns affect water availability, infrastructure, livelihoods, and ecosystem stability, underscoring the need for resilient and climate-adapted physical works.

Document.project_name: Paul First Nation All-Weather Road Access and Rehabilitation Project
Document.description: Paul First Nation is proposing the rehabilitation of existing road segments. Project scope includes targeted gravel road repair and stabilization methods on sections (approximately 2 kilometers) of road in 9 locations on Wabamun 133A.

Document.project_name: Regional Assessment of Oil and Gas Exploratory Drilling in the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Area
Document.description:
The Impact Assessment Agency of Canada will work in close collaboration with Nova Scotia Department of Energy, Natural Resources Canada, and the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Energy Regulator to conduct a regional assessment of exploratory oil and gas drilling in the offshore area of Nova Scotia. The assessment will build on the Regional Assessment of Offshore Wind Development in Nova Scotia (2025) and incorporate relevant learnings from the Regional Assessment of Offshore Oil and Gas Exploratory Drilling East of Newfoundland and Labrador (2020). The regional assessment will serve as a valuable tool to examine the overarching effects of future development activities and inform the federal impact assessment process for offshore oil and gas projects thereby supporting environmental protection and responsible economic development in Nova Scotia.

Please note that this regional assessment was formerly known as the Regional Assessment of Exploratory Oil and Gas Drilling in the Offshore Area of Nova Scotia. The title of the regional assessment has been adjusted to better reflect the activity and to recognize the joint jurisdiction of the offshore area.

Document.project_name: Floating Dock Relocation at Rose Blanche SCH, NL
Document.proponent: Fisheries and Oceans Canada - Small Craft Harbours (DFO-SCH)
location: The Rose Blanche  SCH is located in the community of Rose Blanche-Harbour le Cou , Newfoundland.
Document.description: The proposed project at Rose Blanche SCH includes the relocation of a floating dock. The existing floating dock and its associated anchors, will be removed from the south end of the wharf and relocated to the north end where it will be attached to an existing floating dock and subsequently anchored in place.

Document.project_name: Floating Dock Relocation at Harbour Round SCH, NL
Document.proponent: Fisheries and Oceans Canada - Small Craft Harbours (DFO-SCH)
location: The Harbour Round SCH is located in the community of Harbour Round, Newfoundland.

Two floating docks, or a singular floating dock system, will be moved to the approximate mid-point of the northern marginal wharf and installed perpendicularly. The floating dock system will be floated over to its new location and anchored in place.

Document.project_name: Bedford Channel Dredge Material Placement on McMillan Island IR6
Document.description:
Seyem' Qwantlen Resources Ltd. (Seyem), a wholly owned subsidiary of Kwantlen First Nation, are proposing a new subdivision on McMillan Island IR 6, east of Glover Road. The scope of this project includes tree clearing and the placement of dredge materials on the future subdivision lot. The project area is approximately 15 ha.

Approximately 188,000 m3 to 376,000 m2 of sand will be dredged and hydraulically conveyed to the southside of McMillan Island by floating and/or submerged pipelines. Dredge materials will be transported to the subdivision lot via one of two potential methods: 1) piped directly to the subdivision site, and 2) piped to a stockpile location for dewatering, then trucked to the subdivision lot.

The proponent has applied to Environment and Climate Change Canada for a Species at Risk Act permit under section 73(3).

Document.project_name: Sunrise Expansion Program
Document.description:
Westcoast Energy Inc. (Westcoast) is proposing the Sunrise Expansion Program in British Columbia. This project involves building approximately 137 kilometres (km) of 42-inch diameter natural gas pipeline, extending southwest of Chetwynd to the Canada-United States border near Sumas, British Columbia. The expansion includes several components:


	Eleven pipeline looping segments alongside the existing Westcoast right-of-way, where practical.
	New compressor units at four existing compressor station sites, including electric-driven units and substations at three sites.
	Two new overhead power lines to power the electric-driven compressor units. These total approximately 10 km in length.
	Facility upgrades and other work at 11 existing compressor station sites.
	New piping and equipment at an existing meter station.
	Decommissioning (and removing) 350 metres of previously deactivated pipeline.


Westcoast plans to route the CS-8B to CS9 pipeline loop through Seabird Island Band and Cheam First Nation reserve lands. Westcoast also requires temporary workspace on McLeod Lake Indian Band reserve lands at the northern end of the CS-3 to CS-4B pipeline loop. These reserve lands are federal lands, as defined in section 2 of the Impact Assessment Act. 

In accordance with section 82 of the Impact Assessment Act, the Commission of the Canada Energy Regulator and Environment and Climate Change Canada will each individually determine whether the portion of the project located on federal lands is likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects.

Document.project_name: Transformer Replacement - Fallowfield Road
Document.description: This project involves the replacement of transformer T1 at the Canadian Food inspection Agency site on Fallowfield Road. The existing transformer is from 1972 and is past end of life. The work includes electrical maintenance to continue operations at the campus, including removal of the old equipment and installation and testing of the new transformer.

Document.project_name: Municipal Upgrades – Manston Crescent/Jaeger Way – 22 Wing North Bay
Document.description:
The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. DND is upgrading underground municipal infrastructure along Manston Crescent, Jaeger Way and a walkway between Former Military Police Headquarters (Building 64) and Parker Avenue at 22 Wing North Bay to replace aging infrastructure and to maintain existing hydraulic capacity and ensure long-term service reliability.

The following municipal upgrades are expected:


	Resurfacing of Manston Crescent and Jaeger Way, as well as resurfacing of the existing parking lot south of Jaegar Way.
	Removal and reinstatement of existing curbs, gutters, sidewalks, and boulevard within project area.
	Islands between Jaegar Way and the parking lots will be widened 1 m.
	Removal and replacement of the pedestrian walkway from Manston Crescent to Building 142.
	Removal of street parking areas in front of Building 7 and north of Building 143.
	Removal and replacement of the pedestrian walkway, including parking lot and pedestrian connection, and removal and replacement of the sanitary line between Building 64 and Parker Avenue.
	Removal and replacement of the existing storm, sanitary and watermain along Manston Crescent and Jaeger Way.
	Removal of existing gate and installation of sliding gate at entrance of B2.


Project areas disturbed by construction activities will be restored through repaving, landscaping, revegetation and contouring with existing grades as required.

Document.project_name: Regional Assessment of Offshore Oil and Gas Exploratory Drilling East of Newfoundland and Labrador
Document.description: The Regional Assessment of Offshore Oil and Gas Exploratory Drilling East of Newfoundland and Labrador was completed in February 2020. The assessment sought to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of the assessment process for offshore exploratory drilling projects in the study area while at the same time ensuring that the highest standards of environmental protection continued to be applied and maintained. In response to the recommendations in the Regional Assessment Final Report, the Government of Canada is proceeding with the development and implementation of a Regional Assessment Follow-up Program, which will track and report on the effectiveness of the government's commitments.

Document.project_name: Hiawatha Roadway and Infrastructure Upgrades
Document.description: This project includes the replacement of watermain, sanitary sewer and stormwater underneath Hiawatha Avenue, Hiawatha Crt, and Mahsos Crt, complete with full road reconstruction, curb, and gutter.  Project works are occurring within an existing municipal roadway corridor that is approximately 20m or more from an existing small stream.

Document.project_name: Marten Falls Community Access Road Project
location: Northern end of Painter Lake forestry road
Document.description: Marten Falls First Nation is proposing the construction and operation, including maintenance, of an all-season multi-use community access road approximately 190 to 230 kilometres in length, connecting the northern end of Painter Lake forestry road to the community of Marten Falls. Marten Falls is located at the junction of the Albany and Ogoki rivers, approximately 170 kilometres northeast of Nakina, Ontario. As proposed, the Marten Falls Community Access Road Project could enable future access to potential mineral development activities in the Ring of Fire area.

Document.project_name: Soils Remediation – Garrison Petawawa
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. 4 Canadian Division Support Group (4 CDSG) Environment Services, Garrison Petawawa, is proposing the environmental-compliance driven remediation of contaminated soils in a graveled parking and vehicle/equipment storage compound directly south of 80 Montgomery Road (Building BB-130). Soils characterized as exceeding applicable Federal soil quality guidelines will be removed from the site to a licensed receiving facility.

Document.project_name: River Road and First Street Restoration
Document.description: The project will include roadway reconstruction and drainage upgrades along River Road and First Street. This includes a total length of 514m of roadway reconstruction, installation of new storm sewer infrastructure, ditch grading, with stormwater improvements consisting of both a potential extension of the existing storm sewer system and the construction of a new storm sewer network and outflow pipe. Options are being considered for the outflow.

Document.project_name: Integrated Solid Waste Management System: Landfill Development Project for York Landing, Manitoba
location: Integrated Solid Waste Management System: Landfill Development Project for York Landing, Manitoba
Document.description:
York Factory First Nation (YFFN) proposes to design, construct, and operate an Integrated Solid Waste Management System anchored by a new engineered landfill facility for York Landing, Manitoba. The project will replace the aging and non-compliant waste disposal system and will support current and planned housing growth

The project will be delivered through final planning and capital construction phases. Final planning activities include environmental and geotechnical studies, Indigenous and community engagement, detailed road and landfill construction (IFC) design, and a decommissioning/remediation plan for the existing waste site. Capital work includes site clearing and grading, excavation, access road upgrades/extension, internal roads, landfill cells, leachate collection and lined retention pond, secondary treatment, drainage and surface water controls, passive landfill gas management/methane flaring, waste diversion areas, hazardous waste and e-waste/material sorting storage, organic waste composting, perimeter fencing/security, site signage, solar-powered infrastructure, an operations/storage/inspection building, and a transmission vehicle.

The new facility will include engineered cells with geosynthetic liners and drainage layers, a leachate collection network designed to protect groundwater, and landfill gas controls to reduce methane and odour. The project also includes closure, decommissioning and remediation planning for the existing waste site with long-term groundwater and environmental monitoring. The estimated construction footprint includes approximately 45,000 m2 of vegetation clearing, 15,000 m2 of excavation, and approximately 25,000 m2 of new construction/works.

Document.project_name: 28(2) Blanket Permit - SaskEnergy - Keeseekoose Indian Reserve (Various IR No.)
Document.description:
Natural Gas Low Pressure Distribution Infrastructure - Permit for Blanket Permit for Keeseekoose Indian Reserve KK#66-KE-02, No. 66, No. 66-CA-01, No. 66-CA-02, No. 66-CA-03, No. 66-CA-04, No. 66-CA-05, No. 66-CA-06, No. 66-CA-08, No. 66-CH-01, No. 66-CH-03, No. 66-CH-04, No. 66-CO-01, No. 66-CO-02, No. 66-KE-01, No. 66-KE-02, No. 66-KE-03, No. 66-KE-04, No. 66-KE-05, No. 66-KE-06, No. 66-SA-01, No. 66-SA-02, No. 66-ST-01, No. 66-ST-02, No. 66-ST-03, No. 66A, No. KK# 66-ST-04, No.66-CH-13 for as long as needed.

SaskEnergy may install and maintain natural gas natural gas mains and any supporting infrastructure required to support natural gas distribution services (e.g. meter stations, valves, tie-ins etc.) on above noted reserves. The majority of work will involve the installation, maintenance, repair and decommissioning of mains. Typical work on these projects includes but is not limited to: initial survey of project area, scoping of work, bell hole excavation, exposure of existing mains for tie-ins, installation of mains via trenching/ploughing/directional drilling/boring or other standard means, tie-ins, backfill and re-contouring of excavated or disturbed areas, re-seeding as required, and final clean up of the project area.

Infrastructure installations may also involve topsoil stripping, graveling and grading, building of approaches as required. SaskEnergy infrastructure may be installed adjacent to or within utility corridors that may include power, telecommunications, natural gas transmission, oil, water and/or natural gas distribution. The mains will primarily be installed in land areas that have been subject to previous disturbance, including but not limited to previously cleared cultivated and pasture lands, land developed for residential and rural residential use, urban areas, road verges, and industrial lands. However, portions may also traverse uncleared and/or undeveloped lands and natural landscapes with native plant and wildlife communities.

All construction will follow established standards current at the time of project installation. Potential waste generation includes products of hydrocarbon combustion (e.g. Carbon dioxide), drilling mud (bentonite), potential spills/leaks of materials not limited to hydrocarbons, lubricants, antifreezes and greases typically used in construction equipment. Spill prevention will be emphasized, spill kits used, and clean up and reporting completed following best practices. The Land Manager for the listed IRs will be made aware of all spills.

All SaskEnergy work will involve natural gas and follows established safety standards.

All work will be completed in accordance with the SaskEnergy Environmental Protection Guidelines and will adhere to the Migratory Bird Convention Act and Regulations. Any work for which Keeseekoose First Nation requests engagement, or is of a scale that reasonably warrants wider engagement, will be submitted under separate application. Portions of proposed route which cross heritage sensitive areas and may have the potential to impact cultural, historical or archaeological resources will identified and suitable mitigation will be determined in with the input of the Land Manager.

Document.project_name: Chipewyan Prairie Subdivision Phase 5
Document.description: Chipewyan Prairie First Nation and Indigenous Services Canada are planning to advance subdivision development within the community through the construction of Phase 5. Phase 1 of the subdivision was completed in 2023, adding 16 new lots, and Phase 2 was completed in 2025 with an additional 13 lots. This Environmental Project Description summarizes the results of both a desktop review and a field assessment conducted to identify environmental sensitivities within the proposed Phase 5 subdivision area, with the field visit completed by Associated in October 2025 prior to geotechnical investigations. The Phase 5 subdivision development will include installation of a 200 mm PVC sanitary line and a 200 mm PVC watermain, tying into the existing Phase 1 systems and terminating with end caps at the limits of construction. In addition to deep utilities, the project will involve construction of the internal roadway network with granular road structure, ditches, driveway and residential approaches, and gravel house pads supported by subgrade preparation. Drainage improvements will include the installation of multiple 500 mm and 600 mm CSP culverts with defined slopes. Site preparation will require clearing and grubbing of the development area, topsoil stripping, followed by grading and placement of topsoil to restore disturbed surfaces.

Document.project_name: Improvement of the watertightness and structural integrity of the Carillon lock
Document.description: During the dry docking of the lock at the Carillon Canal National Historic Site in 2024, it was noted that the concrete surfaces of various structures below the waterline were showing signs of deterioration. In fact, the condition of the concrete had deteriorated significantly between 2019 and 2024. The project aims to address the significant civil and mechanical issues related to the watertightness and structural integrity of the lock that were identified.

Document.project_name: Pier 2-5 rehabilitation - CN Fraser River rail bridge
location: Pier 2-5 rehabilitation - CN Fraser River rail bridge
Document.description:
Canadian National Railway Company (CN) is proposing to rehabilitate (i.e., seismic retrofit upgrades) the in-river Piers 2, 3, 4, and 5 of the CN Fraser River rail bridge at Mile 118.7 on the Yale Subdivision, as the bridge is within a seismically active zone. The bridge is located parallel to and between the old Pattullo Bridge and the new stal??w? as?m (Riverview) Bridge in the Fraser River Estuary, between Surrey and New Westminster. Pier 2 is located outside federal lands.

The rehabilitation design for Piers 3 and 4 differs at each location but is based on an integrated sleeve frame system that is supported and bounded by a series of 1,524 mm diameter steel pipes strengthened with rebar and concrete. The frame system will be connected to the existing masonry and each concrete pier shaft above the waterline. Approximately 16 piles will be required: 6 piles for Pier 3 and 10 piles for Pier 4. In addition, composite marine timber walers will be installed at Pier 3 and 4 to mitigate any potential vessel collision. Temporary work platforms will be installed around each pier to facilitate construction activities, including temporary piles to support the frame system. Riprap removal surrounding existing piers may be required if piles cannot be driven through riprap. Riprap will be temporarily relocated out of the immediate work area to allow for pile installation, after which the original riprap will be reinstated around the installed pile.

The rehabilitation design for Pier 5 includes steel rings and struts that will be connected to the existing fender piling. Work below the waterline at Pier 5 is not anticipated. Work barges may be required for material delivery and installation of steel rings and struts. These activities may temporarily affect vessel movements in either the North or South Navigation Channels.

Construction is anticipated to commence in summer 2026 and be completed by the end of 2027. The work will be conducted in a manner consistent with the previously completed seismic retrofits at Pier 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.

Document.project_name: Windfall Mining Project
Document.description: Windfall Mining Group Inc., a subsidiary of Gold Fields Limited, is proposing the construction, operation and decommissioning of a new underground gold mine. The site would be located approximately 115 km east of Lebel-sur-Quévillon, in the Nord-du-Québec region, in Quebec. The project would have an ore production capacity of 4,950  tons per day and an approximate mine life of 10 years. The project would include two underground access ramps (tunnels), an ore processing plant with a processing capacity of 4,080 tons per day, facilities for the management of mine waste and tailings, and a camp for approximately 600 workers.

Document.project_name: 2024 - 2034 Eastern Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Exploration Drilling Project - Excluded Physical Activities
responsible_authority: Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Petroleum Board
Document.description: ExxonMobil Canada Ltd. is proposing to conduct an exploration drilling project within its offshore exploration license located about 500 kilometres northeast of St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador in the Atlantic Ocean. As proposed, the 2024 – 2034 Eastern Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Exploration Drilling Project would allow the proponent to determine the presence, nature, and quantity of potential hydrocarbon resources within the exploration license 1169. The exploration will take place over a nine-year period.

Document.project_name: ATCO Spray River Replace
Document.description: The Spray River Replacement Project will upgrade a section of the Banff Transmission Line between the Spray River crossing and Banff Gate Station to enable in-line inspection and improve maintenance. The river crossing will be replaced using horizontal directional drilling, while other sections will be installed by open-cut methods. A temporary steel bypass pipeline will maintain gas service during construction. The existing 1951 pipeline will be cleaned, grouted, capped, and abandoned in place. Access will be via the ATCO East Gate and green spaces near the Spray River golf course bridge. The project is located on lands managed by both Parks Canada Agency and the Town of Banff.

Document.project_name: Trans Mountain Miette River Encroachment 2 (KP386.75)
Document.description: This project will be assessed with a basic impact assessment. Trans Mountain Pipeline ULC is proposing a bank armouring project along a 40-metre section of the Miette River in Jasper National Park. Ground inspections identified a geohazard at pipeline KP386.75, where the eroded Miette riverbank is now only 2.9 m from the Line 1 pipeline. If no action is taken, continuing erosion by the river could expose the pipeline within two years. The goal of the project is to prevent further encroachment of the river towards the pipeline to protect the line from being exposed and damaged in the future. Trans Mountain plans to achieve this by installing rip rap apron and a raised earthen bank where the river has eroded the slope by the pipeline. The project will require access along the pipeline right-of-way, temporary workspace in a previously disturbed area and disturbance of 1-2 hectares to construct the riprap apron and berm. The work is tentatively planned for fall 2026 and will take a small workforce about one month to complete.

Document.project_name: Replacement of the outhouses in Quarry Bay with urine-diverting dry toilets
Document.description:
The Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve must replace the outhouses in Quarry Bay, which have reached the end of their useful life. In addition to the latrines, the facilities at Quarry Bay include a dock, a kitchen shelter, 6 oTENTik campsites, and 8 backcountry campsites. The site is designated as a front-country campground.

The outhouses will be dismantled and replaced with urine-diverting dry toilets. The targeted areas are already largely disturbed by the existing outhouses. The new facilities will require a minor expansion of the disturbed area. This will involve clearing vegetation, removing the organic soil layer (approximately 10 m² per site), installing an infiltration trench, and then installing the prefabricated structures on site.

Document.project_name: Ashwell Road Development Project
Document.description:
The Proposed Project

Westbow Construction Group (Westbow) is proposing to develop the southern portion of the Kwaw-Kwaw-Apilt First Nation lands, in Chilliwack, BC into a residential community. The proposal includes constructing townhouses, apartments, roads, a school, and associated infrastructure. It also involves infilling of sections of Waterlily Slough, clearing riparian habitat, constructing a gravel amenity path, installing stormwater outfalls, and installing an arch culvert bridge over Waterlily Diversion Slough.

 

In total, approximately 2,600 m2 of instream habitat and 12,000 m2 of riparian habitat will be impacted. Habitat offsetting is included in the proposal to counterbalance these impacts. The proposed offsetting focuses on enhancements to on-site aquatic and riparian areas. A wetted backwater feature off of Chilliwack Creek will be constructed within the wetland areas of the Waterlily Slough Diversion Channel. Additionally, the lower section of Waterlily Slough will be enhanced through the construction of multiple pool habitat features and the removal of fish barriers and anthropogenic debris.

Document.project_name: Replacement of the septic systems at Sites 3 and 4 at the Falls Lake Cottages and Campground, Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Halifax
Document.description: Canadian Forces Morale and Welfare Services (CFMWS) is proposing a project. CFMWS is proposing the replacement of aging septic systems at Sites 3 and 4 of the Falls Lake Cottages and Campground, Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Halifax, due to the end of their service life. The project is intended to maintain reliable wastewater management infrastructure and support the continued operation of the campground facilities. The existing septic tank at Site 3 is located approximately 62 ft (18.9 m) from the water's edge, while the existing septic tanks at Site 4 are located approximately 96 ft (29.3 m) from the water's edge. The project will occur on previously developed land and will involve the replacement of the existing pump chambers at both Sites 3 and 4, while the existing septic tanks will remain in place. In addition, an extra septic chamber will be installed at Site 4 to increase system capacity. Construction activities may include excavation, installation of prefabricated components, trenching for new or existing utilities, and tie-ins to communications, water, sanitary, and electrical infrastructure, as required. Construction is anticipated to occur in late fall 2026. The project will result in an increase in wastewater system capacity through the addition and replacement of septic chambers; however, it will not involve a change in land use, campground footprint, or the overall function of the site.

Document.project_name: Yellowhead Copper Project
Document.description:
Trekor Metals Limited is proposing the construction, operation, and closure of a new open-pit copper mine located about 150 kilometres northeast of Kamloops, British Columbia. The Yellowhead Copper Project has been designed with a production capacity of 90,000 tonnes of ore per day (up to 32 million tonnes per year) over a 25-year mine life. The project, which would also produce gold and silver, includes a new mill, an approximately 110 kilometre transmission line that would connect to an existing BC Hydro substation near 100 Mile House, and a rail load-out facility at an existing site at Vavenby.

British Columbia's Environmental Assessment Office is collaborating with the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada as part of the federal impact assessment of the project. For more information on the EAO's process, please visit EPIC.engage.

 

Please note that the proponent of this project was previously known as Taseko Mines Limited.

Document.project_name: Women Pro-Forests: Climate Change Adaptation in the Moyen-Bafing National Park
location: Developed land of the Moyen-Bafing National Park in Guinea
Document.description:
This project aims to improve climate change adaptation for women, young women, and their families in the Moyen-Bafing National Park. Achieving this objective relies on the increased adoption of nature-based solutions that support biodiversity, for the benefit of women and young women. The project seeks to sustainably improve the economic opportunities of beneficiaries through nature-based, climate-smart agroforestry solutions that are respectful of forest biodiversity. It also aims to strengthen inclusive and equitable governance of forest biodiversity in support of adaptation to climate change for women, vulnerable young women, and their families.

Project activities notably include support for community-based reforestation and forest corridor and habitat restoration programs in key areas of the Moyen-Bafing National Park; the establishment of support services to help remove barriers to climate change adaptation related to unpaid care work; and the provision of training on feminist climate justice and women's environmental rights.

The project includes the following physical activities and infrastructures:

1) Development of 21 Farmer Field Schools (FFS):

FFSs are collective learning sites aimed at promoting nature-based solutions for vegetable and food crop production. They include:


	Preparation of agricultural plots with an area of 902 m² (41 m × 22 m), including selective clearing of herbaceous and shrubby vegetation, spot stump removal where necessary, and site clearing (removal of stones, branches, and debris).
	Installation of a temporary wire-mesh protective fence around each plot, with a perimeter of 126 meters and a height of 1.50 m, supported by wooden or metal posts, to protect plots from livestock intrusion and wildlife. The gradual establishment of living hedges is planned to replace the fences in the medium term (3 to 5 years).
	Ridging and installation of drainage channels and temporary soak pits for the management of rainwater and irrigation water.
	Sowing and transplanting of vegetable or food crops, as well as soil mulching.
	Type of land: existing or fallow agricultural land that has already been developed and is known to local communities, located within the National Park development zone (away from high-biodiversity and conservation areas).


2) Development of 7 Farmer Beekeeping Schools (FBS):

FBSs are collective learning sites aimed at promoting nature-based solutions for honey production. They include:


	Light clearing of plots with an area of 2,500 m² (50 m × 50 m), without clearing or stump removal, in order to preserve vegetation beneficial to pollinators.
	Installation of a temporary wire-mesh protective fence around each plot, with a perimeter of 200 meters and a height of 1.50 m, supported by wooden or metal posts, to protect plots from livestock intrusion and wildlife. The gradual establishment of living hedges is planned to replace the fences in the medium term (3 to 5 years).
	Installation of Kenyan top-bar hives (25 hives per FBS), placed on metal stands approximately 1.5 m above the ground to protect colonies and facilitate management.
	Type of land: agricultural or semi-developed land, often located along the edges of wooded areas favorable to beekeeping, within the National Park development zone (away from high-biodiversity and conservation areas).


3) Construction of 4 shea butter production hubs (processing of shea nuts), in 4 different villages, each comprising:


	A shelter: a building with a total area of 80 m² for storage and warehousing, also serving as office space.
	Drying area: an adjacent outdoor concrete surface with an area of 45 m², enclosed by a fence to protect products from animals, with a height of 2 meters and a total length of 52 meters.
	Concrete sludge-drying structure: area of 18 m², comprising one settling basin, one water recovery basin, one sludge collection basin, and one drying bed.
	Type of land: developed land located within villages, situated in the National Park development zone (away from conservation areas).


4) Fencing for the protection of 3 vegetable production plots, each plot including:


	Installation of a wire-mesh fence 700 meters in length and 2 meters in height to secure a 3-hectare vegetable farming perimeter.
	Type of land: existing or fallow agricultural land that has already been developed and is known to local communities, located within the National Park development zone (away from high-biodiversity and conservation areas).


5) Construction of 4 honey production centers, in 4 villages, each comprising:


	A shelter: a building with a total area of 80 m² for product storage and warehousing, also serving as office space.
	Type of land: developed land located within villages, situated in the National Park development zone (away from conservation areas).


6) Rehabilitation of 2 potable water points (existing wells and boreholes), including:


	Improvement and rehabilitation of the drinking water supply system from a borehole in Téguéréya Centre village, including relocation of an elevated water tank, installation of a solar pump, and installation of public standpipes.
	Extension of the borehole distribution network with the installation of a drinking water supply system for a vegetable production plot in the village of Ley Kimbili.


7) Construction of 7 new irrigation boreholes, with two design options depending on the results of yield tests. The first option would include a borehole equipped with a solar pump and a water conveyance system that may exceed 100 meters in length to deliver water to agricultural plots. The second option would include a borehole equipped with a hand pump and an adjacent elevated water tank.


	Type of land: all new boreholes will be located near the agricultural infrastructures planned within the shea and/or honey development hubs. These sites are accessible via existing tracks (developed land). Land zoning: public land located within the PNMB development zone and therefore without protected status.


The project also includes the repair of 12 additional potable water boreholes and the construction of two storage facilities for vegetable products, each with an area of 80 m², on developed land. These structures are not subject to the law, as they comply with the conditions and thresholds described in the Ministerial Exclusion Order.

The intervention area of the Femmes Pro Forêts (FproF) project corresponds to the boundaries of the Moyen-Bafing National Park (PNMB) in Guinea. These are areas where infrastructure development is permitted and are characterized by:


	a tropical climate marked by a prolonged dry season and an intense rainy season, with annual rainfall between 1,500 and 2,000 mm and temperatures ranging from 10 to 33 °C;
	clay-loam, sandy-clay, or organic-matter-rich soils suitable for food and vegetable crops;
	vegetation cover composed of shrub savannas, secondary forests, and agricultural fallows.


All installations will be located outside areas of high ecological value and fully protected zones of the PNMB, as well as on previously used or developed land, without the need for expropriation or heavy construction. Implementation of the works will comply with Guinean environmental regulations and with good agricultural and apicultural practices in rural areas.

Phase 2 Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) and Marker's Shelter Demolition - Amherst Rifle Range, Nova-Scotia
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) has proposed a project. The proposed Phase 2 Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) work at the Amherst Rifle Range, located on Willow Street in Amherst, Nova Scotia, will consist of the construction of three boreholes, all of which will be installed as overburden monitoring wells (approximate depth of 6 metres). Each drilling location will require selective tree and brush clearing, as needed, to provide safe access for the drill rig and associated equipment to reach the proposed borehole locations. The proposed Marker's Shelter demolition work will consist of mechanical demolition of the concrete structure (e.g., hydraulic breaker, grapple), including minor excavation of earthen materials to fully expose the structure, breaking and processing of all concrete and reinforcing steel (rebar), and disposal at an approved construction and demolition (C&D) facility. Backfilling and grading of the work area, as required, using suitable on-site or imported materials to restore site conditions and safe final grades is included in the scope. The work is expected to take place Fall 2026, pending final determination and identification of appropriate mitigation measures.
